arxiv-1905-10715.title: Graph Attention Auto-Encoders DOI: 10.475/123_4 ISBN: 123-4567-24-567/08/06 4 Price: 15.00
arxiv-1905-10715.creator: Amin Salehi, Hasan Davulcu
arxiv-1905-10715.description: Abstract . Auto-encoders have emerged as a successful framework for unsupervised learning. However, conventional auto-encoders are incapable of utilizing explicit relations in structured data. To take advantage of relations in graph-structured data, several graph auto-encoders have recently been proposed, but they neglect to reconstruct either the graph structure or node attributes.

arxiv-2207-14795.creator: Krishnanand Mallayya 1 , Joshua Straquadine 2 , Matthew J. Krogstad 3,4 , Maja D. Bachmann 2 , Anisha G. Singh 2 , Raymond Osborn 3 , Stephan Rosenkranz 3 , Ian R. Fisher 2 , Eun-Ah Kim 1,5∗ 1 Department of Physics, Cornell University, Ithaca, NY 14853, USA 2 Geballe Laboratory for Advanced Material
arxiv-2207-14795.description: Abstract The Bragg glass phase is a nearly perfect crystal with glassy features predicted to occur in vortex lattices and charge density wave systems in the presence of disorder. Detecting it has been challenging despite its sharp theoretical definition in terms of diverging correlation lengths.

arxiv-2305-03446.title: A construction of deformations to general algebras
arxiv-2305-03446.creator: Dave Bowman, Dora Puljić, Agata Smoktunowicz
arxiv-2305-03446.description: Abstract One of the questions investigated in deformation theory is to determine to which algebras can a given associative algebra be deformed. In this paper we investigate a different but related question, namely: for a given associative finite-dimensional ℂ \mathbb{C} -algebra A A , find algebras N N which can be deformed to A A .

arxiv-2405-00480.title: Better Bounded Bisimulation Contractions (Preprint)
arxiv-2405-00480.creator: Thomas Bolander, Alessandro Burigana
arxiv-2405-00480.description: Abstract Bisimulations are standard in modal logic and, more generally, in the theory of state-transition systems. The quotient structure of a Kripke model with respect to the bisimulation relation is called a bisimulation contraction. The bisimulation contraction is a minimal model bisimilar to the original model, and hence, for (image-)finite models, a minimal model modally equivalent to the original.

arxiv-2508-20983.title: Multilingual Dataset Integration Strategies for Robust Audio Deepfake Detection: A SAFE Challenge System
arxiv-2508-20983.creator: Hashim Ali, Surya Subramani, Lekha Bollinani, Nithin Sai Adupa, Sali El-Loh, Hafiz Malik
arxiv-2508-20983.description: Abstract The SAFE Challenge evaluates synthetic speech detection across three tasks: unmodified audio, processed audio with compression artifacts, and laundered audio designed to evade detection. We systematically explore self-supervised learning (SSL) front-ends, training data compositions, and audio length configurations for robust deepfake detection.

arxiv-2510-17098.title: Can Transformer Memory Be Corrupted? Investigating Cache-Side Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models
arxiv-2510-17098.description: Abstract Even when prompts and parameters are secured, transformer language models remain vulnerable because their key–value (KV) cache during inference constitutes an overlooked attack surface. To address this, we present MTI V.1, a modular framework that formalizes and implements the Malicious Token Injection (MTI) attack.

arxiv-2511-15167.title: Learning Depth from Past Selves: Self-Evolution Contrast for Robust Depth Estimation
arxiv-2511-15167.creator: Jing Cao, Kui Jiang, Shenyi Li, Xiaocheng Feng, Yong Huang
arxiv-2511-15167.description: Abstract Self-supervised depth estimation has gained significant attention in autonomous driving and robotics. However, existing methods exhibit substantial performance degradation under adverse weather conditions such as rain and fog, where reduced visibility critically impairs depth prediction. To address this issue, we propose a novel self-evolution contrastive learning framework called SEC-Depth for self-supervised robust depth estimation tasks.

arxiv-2602-04845.title: QMUL-PH-26-04 Finite-dimensional algebras, gauge-string duality and thermodynamics.
arxiv-2602-04845.creator: Sanjaye Ramgoolam
arxiv-2602-04845.description: Abstract Gauge-invariant polynomial functions of matrix and tensor variables capture combinatorial structures of gauge-string duality, which can be usefully organised using finite-dimensional associative algebras. I review recent work on eigenvalue systems using these algebras as state spaces, which provide efficient computational algorithms for the construction of orthogonal bases for multi-matrix invariants.

pmc-11484361.title: Adherence to a low-fat dietary pattern reduces head and neck cancer risk: evidence from the PLCO trial

pmc-11484361.description: PurposeLow-fat dietary (LFD) pattern refers to a dietary structure with reduced fat intake. pmc-11620035.title: Spectrum of DNA variants for patients with hearing loss in 4 language families of 15 ethnicities from Southwestern China
pmc-11620035.creator: Jingyu Li, Shiyu Zhou, Jiahong Pei, Wanzhen Li, Rongjie Cui, Xiaofei Ren, Jingru Wei, Qian Li, Baosheng Zhu, Yaliang Sa, Yunlong Li
pmc-11620035.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Hearing loss is a common disease. More than 100 genes have been reported to be associated with hereditary hearing loss. However, the distribution of these genes and their variants across diverse populations remains unclear. In this study, we gathered 347 hearing-impaired patients from four language families (Sinitic, Tibeto-Burman, Kra-Dai, and Hmong-Mien) in Southwestern China, excluding cases caused by common mutations in the GJB2 gene. By using next generation sequencing, 122 genes associated with hereditary hearing loss were analyzed on these patients.

pmc-13373531.title: Causal Associations of Heparin‐Binding Growth and Differentiation Factors With Thyroid Cancer: A Two‐Sample Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-13373531.creator: Xiwei Zhang, Dongqiang Yang, Yan Liu, Yanzhao Wu, Ping Shi
pmc-13373531.description: BackgroundHeparin‐binding growth and differentiation factors (GDFs) play roles in various cellular processes and are potential contributors to thyroid cancer. Although population‐based studies have documented associations between heparin‐binding GDFs and thyroid cancer, their causal relationships remain unclear.MethodsA two‐sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was conducted using published genome‐wide association studies (GWASs) data.

pmc-13402105.title: Risk factor analysis and prediction model construction for delayed erythroid hematopoietic reconstitution after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a single-center retrospective study
pmc-13402105.creator: Qianqian Zhang, Fangfang Ge, Lijie Han, Mengmeng Yan, Rong Guo, Zhongxing Jiang
pmc-13402105.description: BackgroundAllogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) represents a potential therapeutic option for various hematological disorders. With continuous advancement in transplantation techniques and the expansion of indications, clinical issues associated with delayed erythroid hematopoietic reconstitution (DEHR) have become increasingly prominent.MethodsThis retrospective study identified independent risk factors through univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, subsequently constructing a prediction model.

pmc-13454591.title: Nos1 neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamic area modulate lipid metabolism via the sympathetic nervous system in male mice
pmc-13454591.creator: Kunio Kondoh, Emi Hashiuchi, Yuka Inaba, Hiroshi Inoue, Serika Yamada, Kazunari Miyamichi, Yuki Yoshimura, Ken-ichiro Nakajima, Takeshi Y. Hiyama, Yasuhiko Minokoshi
pmc-13454591.description: The selection of the appropriate energy substrate under different physiological conditions is a key aspect of the energy metabolism homeostasis. We here show that Nos1 (nitric oxide synthase 1)-expressing cells in the paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVH) serve as a pivotal node for controlling whole-body fat consumption in male mice.

pmc-13466064.title: An efficient lattice-based identity-based proxy Re-encryption scheme with direct revocation for cloud storage
pmc-13466064.creator: Juanjuan Li, Mingming Jiang, Yuyan Guo
pmc-13466064.description: As cloud storage becomes increasingly commonplace alongside the expansion of data sharing practices, how to achieve secure data sharing and user revocation while ensuring data confidentiality has become a key issue. Proxy re-encryption enables ciphertext originally designated for one user to be transformed by a semi-trusted proxy for another user, while identity-based encryption offers a simplified approach to key administration.

pmc-13590040.title: Unpacking Multimodal Verb Input in English: Insights From Typically Developing Infants and Those Who are Deaf and Hard of Hearing
pmc-13590040.creator: Feile Meng, Isobel Horsfall‐Turner, Cassim Hussain, Iris Nomikou, Rana Abu‐Zhaya
pmc-13590040.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study offers a descriptive account of multimodal verb input to Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) and Typically Developing (TD) infants across crucial points in verb acquisition. Using the North American English Ambrose (2016) corpus, we analysed mother‐infant play interactions at 13 and 22 months, and explored caregivers' verb input, its combination with caregiver action and in response to infant action.
